        ### Question
        Which of the following analytical determinations is less useful for decision making in the follow-up and control of an HIV-infected person?

        ### Options
        opa. CD4 lymphocyte count in peripheral blood.
opb. Quantification of immunoglobulin.
opc. Measurement of viral load.
opd. Studies of HIV resistance to antiretroviral drugs.
ope. Analysis of the co-receptor tropism.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: CD4 lymphocyte count in peripheral blood -> provides information on immune status -> crucial for monitoring HIV progression -> 95% CHAIN: Quantification of immunoglobulin -> assesses overall immune function -> important but less specific for HIV management -> 80% CHAIN: Measurement of viral load -> indicates HIV replication activity -> essential for monitoring treatment efficacy -> 98% CHAIN: Studies of HIV resistance to antiretroviral drugs -> guides selection of effective treatment -> critical for personalized therapy -> 90% CHAIN: Analysis of the co-receptor tropism -> determines HIV strain characteristics -> less directly impactful on routine follow-up decisions -> 95%
